blocking.section: ISA §§7.1, 7.4, 10; src/classical.rs::ClassicalMachine::step, especially pending assignment at 1473 and pending.clone() at 1567

steps.claim: §7.1 memory is "Byte-addressed, little-endian, sparse" and alloc succeeds when its bump and table checks pass. §10 requires an in-range hostcall to copy its bytes into the request, and says "the frame records the request bytes, the overwritten bytes and the reply bytes"; §7.4 retains that frame. A 67108864-byte allocation at address 1 in the R21 64-bit layout is legal. Failure to store the required request/history is a reported host-resource limitation, not an ISA range fault or process abort, as in the accepted R21 repair requirement.

The independent complete object changes only the R21 CC constant to n = const.i64 67108864, then p = alloc n; r = hostcall org.bennett.test p n; ret r. Its literal envelope has interface=closure 655e72211b66a9e4e3f8dcaff74c5203da6ec1d834fc43570833f0ab1387a577; object/file SHA-256 is df7f95dd72496eb446c39319d5ef1e6287ebed8fdd6b9a7f92eba31ba1431071. Stock check and hash exit 0. Under RLIMIT_AS=134217728 and RLIMIT_CORE=0, both the public-library probe linked against the built crate and stock run-cc exit -6/SIGABRT with "memory allocation of 67108864 bytes failed". The library prints successful parse/check_hashes and completion of the two prefix instructions before aborting; CLI stdout is empty. Reproduce with the mandatory headless prefix followed by python3 /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-isa-spec-review/.tmp/r22-codex/reproduce.py.

The initial fallible transfer_bytes reservation succeeds. step then sets state.pending to the request. Outside the execute closure and its undo-on-Err path, history construction calls self.state.pending.clone(), whose derived HostRequest clone infallibly clones the full Vec<u8>. GDB identifies Vec<u8>::clone -> HostRequest::clone -> Option<HostRequest>::clone -> ClassicalMachine::step at classical.rs:1567. The second 64-MiB allocation exceeds the process limit and invokes the allocator abort handler. There is no recoverable Result and no rollback. This is the obligatory retention stage of the same text-driven transfer, not an arbitrarily pre-filled resident heap.

The original 2^63 hostcall and console inputs now return cited host-limit Results, leave the full snapshot unchanged, publish no request/tape/output and reverse to entry. Their 0/1/8 controls succeed. At 64 MiB the console control also rejects cleanly at its cumulative console reservation and restores the prefix. R21 large transfer tests always reject before pending construction, explaining why all 436 tests and five sweeps pass despite the unguarded history copy.

S0 core resource-reporting failure: the hostcall repair is incomplete once initial materialization succeeds but required history retention cannot. This prevents both core and whole-crate acceptance. The clone predates this diff, so this is a newly exposed continuation of CODEX-R21-B02, not a regression of a retained pin. It fits no stated theorem of INV-1..INV-5: those proofs do not establish host allocation/error handling for CC request retention. ISA T4 assumes a valid retained trace and does not justify an infallible allocation while constructing one.

The determining §10 words are "those bytes are copied into the request" and "the frame records the request bytes, the overwritten bytes and the reply bytes", together with §7.1 sparse allocation. With the current two-buffer representation the supplied 64-MiB object under 128-MiB RLIMIT_AS must return Err containing §10 and host limit, CLI exit 1 without JSON, with no pending request or history/output delta; reverse must restore the entry snapshot. If storage is shared and the transfer fits, normal successful request creation is valid instead.
